target_customer: Developers building and monetizing autonomous AI agents
problem: Building agents requires reasoning frameworks, state management, analytics and monetization that developers must assemble themselves.
business_model: Developer platform with a marketplace and monetization layer (pricing not found)

founders.name: Scott Moss
founders.background_notes: YC page also says he was a VC.

technical_complexity.rationale: Orchestrating agents with state, pause, rewind and human intervention was standard engineering on LLM APIs; reliability of autonomous work is the hard part.

defensibility.rationale: Agent frameworks were crowded and open source; a marketplace could add network effects only with scale.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Model providers and cloud vendors shipped agent tooling during 2024-2025; Doublezero's outcome is unknown.

market_need_then: Strong developer interest in agents in 2024; no direct evidence of paying demand found.

brand_strength.rationale: Product Hunt beta launch exists but no press on the brand itself.

pivots.from: Superfilter, an AI executive assistant managing inboxes (S24 build)
pivots.why: Not stated; the landing page copyright reads Superfilter Inc. so it is the same company. The founders also launched Ceejay, an inbox assistant.

outcome_analysis: Doublezero is a two-person team that entered S24 as Superfilter, an inbox assistant, and now presents an agent platform; they also run Ceejay. No funding, revenue or user numbers are public, so only the repeated pivoting and crowded agent-platform market can be noted.
notes: No funding data found (VCBacked, Altss and Crunchbase pages had no usable details). YC says founded 2025 though batch is S24. Round Funded page is a reconstructed application and was ignored.
